faqs.q: Sec. 66-61. - Park permit fees for groups consuming 3.2 beer.
faqs.a:
(a)
There is hereby imposed a $15.00 permit fee for groups of people who consume 3.2 fermented
               malt beverages in any public park facility in the city.
(b)
Consumption of 3.2 fermented malt beverages by permit issued pursuant to subsection
               (a) of this section is limited to the following public park facilities in the city:
               Pioneer Pavilion, North Jeffco West Park, Allen House Pavilion, Oak Park, Oak Park
               Pavilion, Lutz Sports Complex, Youth Memorial Complex, and Arvada Tennis Center, Mechelen
               Pavilion Memorial Park, and McIlvoy Park Pavilion.
(c)
The Director of Parks, Golf and Hospitality Services is authorized to grant a written
               permit for consumption of 3.2 fermented malt beverages upon public park facilities
               in the city, subject to the provisions of chapter 6 and subject to the following provisions:
(1)
The permittee is a natural person who is 21 years of age or older;
(2)
The permittee agrees to remain with the group so long as 3.2 fermented malt beverages
               are consumed by any member of the group;
(3)
The permittee agrees to maintain the noise level of the group within the limits established
               by
section 38-91
relating to maximum permissible continuous sound pressure levels;
(4)
The permittee agrees to pay the cost of cleaning or the cost of repair of any damage
               of the public park facility; and
(5)
The permittee agrees that the group will transport and consume 3.2 fermented malt
               beverages in nonglass containers.
(d)
Any permit for the consumption of 3.2 fermented malt beverages granted by the director
               of parks, golf and hospitality services is valid only between the hours of 11:00 a.m.
               and 9:00 p.m. on the day for which the city manager grants the permit.
(e)
Any permit granted by the director of parks, golf and hospitality services for the
               consumption of 3.2 fermented malt beverages in public park facilities may be revoked
               by the director of parks, golf and hospitality services or a designee thereof for
               good cause shown. The term "good cause shown" means a violation by the permittee or
               any member of the permittee's group of this section, of any other terms and conditions
               of the permit granted by the director of parks, golf and hospitality services, or
               chapter 6, or of any law or ordinance.
(Code 1981, § 2-197; Ord. No. 2516, § 1, 6-6-1988; Ord. No. 3883, § 1, 6-7-2004)
